A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same study with the same title and authors. All 17 pages of each version, including figures, equations, tables and Appendices A–B, support reliable comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original multilingual memorization measurements, graph correlations, model comparisons and sensitivity analyses in Section 6 and Appendix B.

after.justification: v2 retains these original empirical results, including the main result tables and appendix analyses and generation examples.

M1.justification: Language-subspace extraction, memorization measures, thresholded graph construction, Laplacian correlation and intra-/cross-topology aggregation remain unchanged. Appendix A retains the same algorithm.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same mC4 memorization data, Flores+ language representations, language sets and completion/reconstruction tasks. The Lang2Vec and ASJP comparisons in Appendix B.4 are also retained.

E2.justification: Pearson correlation remains the comparator for the proposed graph correlation, with unchanged model comparisons. Newly cited ROME and forgetting-curve methods appear only in related work, not as evaluated baselines.

E3.justification: The filtering, mC4 sampling, prompt-length conditions, 15-token targets, model sizes and threshold sweeps remain unchanged. The new Flores+ sample-count statement documents the existing setup without reporting a protocol revision.

E4.justification: The threshold sweeps, prompt-length and model-scale analyses, layer-wise similarity comparisons, memorization examples and unstable-generation case remain unchanged. The added threshold limitation introduces no new robustness experiment.

E5.justification: Statistical reporting is unchanged. v2 adds no repeated-run or seed information, confidence intervals, significance tests or uncertainty-estimation procedures.

E6.justification: The main and appendix numerical results, plotted trends and generation examples are retained. For example, Table 1 still reports MGPT-101 graph correlations of -0.24 for EM and -0.56 for PM. Table 5 changes model labels, not results.

T1.justification: The memorization definitions, graph smoothness and cross-smoothness formulas, correlation coefficient and Cauchy-Schwarz bound, and subgraph aggregation equations remain unchanged.

C1.justification: Both claim a first large-scale multilingual memorization study, a language-similarity graph correlation, and higher memorization with fewer training tokens among similar languages. The revised abstract clarifies the monolingual-focus motivation without changing these contributions or their scope.

C2.justification: v2 newly acknowledges sensitivity to manually selected similarity thresholds and limited applicability to dissimilar languages that become isolated nodes. It suggests adaptive or threshold-free alternatives while retaining the earlier limitation concerning unexamined fine-tuning effects.

D1.justification: Section 4.1 newly states that Flores+ is separate from model training data and contains 2,000 examples per language. Table 5 corrects the 1.2B MT5-BASE label to MT5-LARGE and distinguishes MGPT-1.3B from MGPT-13B. Code-access information is unchanged.

R1.justification: Section 2 adds Chen et al. (2024), Liu et al. (2024), Li et al. (2024a), Haviv et al. (2022), Stoehr et al. (2024) and Zhao et al. (2024). These extend discussion of memorization mechanisms, measurement and language structure while retaining the central research positioning.

P1.justification: The abstract and introduction receive limited clarification; related work, limitations and acknowledgements expand. Terminology and model labels are corrected, but the section sequence and most scientific prose remain unchanged.

P2.justification: All figures and tables are retained, with limited layout changes: Figure 3 switches columns, Table 1 moves from page 6 to page 7, and Figure 4 and Table 4 shift position. Table 4's caption is shortened, and printed page numbers are removed.

improvement.justification: v2 improves transparency through the Flores+ disclosure and corrected model identification, and better qualifies applicability by acknowledging threshold sensitivity and isolated-language limitations omitted from v1. Expanded related work adds useful context. The method and empirical evidence, including appendix results, remain unchanged, making the overall gain limited to documentation, positioning and qualification.
